## Summary

The May 6, 2026 acceptance guide covers three surfaces for UPI in India: Checkout, Elements with the Checkout Sessions API and Elements with the Payment Intents API. The customer authenticates on their mobile device and approves the payment or future charges. The May Checkout and Payment Intents Elements sections describe immediate success or failure notification for one-off payments and cases where the method is saved for future use, and delayed notification for off-session or recurring payments when the customer is absent.

## May integration paths

- **Checkout.** The guide lists US, EU, CA, GB, AU, SG and CH business locations and requires INR for all line items. It describes payment, setup and subscription modes and recurring UPI AutoPay e-mandates. Dynamic configuration is available. For manual configuration, add `upi` to `payment_method_types`. The hosted example uses `success_url`, and the embedded-page example uses `return_url`. The Checkout section says a QR code expires five minutes after creation, at which point Stripe emits `payment_intent.payment_failed` and the expired code cannot complete the payment.
- **Elements with Checkout Sessions API.** The merchant's server creates the Session and returns its client secret. All line items use INR. The guide describes dynamic Dashboard management and manual method listing. The May HTML/JS path loads Stripe.js directly from `js.stripe.com` and uses `initCheckoutElementsSdk`. If loading as an npm module, the HTML/JS instructions specify `@stripe/stripe-js` 7.0.0 or later. The May React path uses `CheckoutElementsProvider` and specifies `@stripe/react-stripe-js` 5.0.0 or later and `@stripe/stripe-js` 8.0.0 or later (May raw lines 218–246). The client confirms via the Checkout instance or its actions. This section describes a 24-hour Checkout Session lifetime, separate from the five-minute UPI QR window.
- **Elements with Payment Intents API.** The server sets the amount and currency on a PaymentIntent and provides its client secret to Elements. The May guide requires HTTPS for live checkout. The client secret can complete the payment, so the merchant keeps it out of logs and merchant-constructed URLs and provides it only to the customer (May raw lines 716–730, 763–765). The client uses `stripe.confirmPayment` with `return_url`. Stripe appends the PaymentIntent ID and client secret on its redirect, and the return page retrieves the PaymentIntent and inspects its status (May raw lines 962–971). The status-display examples handle `succeeded`, `processing` and `requires_payment_method`; the redirect itself does not determine the outcome.

The May Checkout and Checkout Sessions Elements tests use a QR code that opens a Stripe-hosted test page with authorize or expire choices. The May Payment Intents Elements branch ends at the instruction to use test API keys. A separate May guide documents Direct API setup and charge-and-save flows under [[source-stripe-upi-set-up-future-payments]].

payments-upi-accept-a-payment.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/upi/accept-a-payment identifies UPI acceptance in India using Payment Intents and Payment Methods APIs and indexes Checkout, Elements with Checkout Sessions, and Elements with Payment Intents (new raw lines 5-16). It contains no detailed prerequisites or state transitions. The May 6 guide says the customer authenticates on mobile and approves a payment or future charges. Checkout uses INR line items, supports payment, setup and subscription, and refers to UPI AutoPay e-mandates. The merchant gets immediate stated success/failure notification for one-off and saving cases and a delayed notification for absent-customer off-session or recurring payments (old raw lines 18-49). In May Checkout, the QR expires after five minutes and triggers the failure event (old raw lines 104-114). In the May Elements routes, the merchant server creates either a Session or an Intent; the client uses the matching object and client secret to confirm, and the Intent route retrieves status on return. The May Checkout Sessions HTML/JS path loads Stripe.js directly from js.stripe.com. Its npm module floor is 7.0.0, while the React branch needs React Stripe.js 5.0.0 and loader 8.0.0 or later (old raw lines 218-246). The May Payment Intents Elements path requires HTTPS for live checkout. Its client secret can complete the charge. Keep it out of merchant-built URLs and logs and share it only with the customer. Separately, Stripe provides Intent query parameters for retrieval on return (old raw lines 716-730, 763-765 and 962-971). A return may show succeeded, processing or a failed state and does not itself verify payment (old raw lines 139-174, 502-541, 603-647, 866-868 and 962-1017). source-stripe-upi-accept-payment.md now retains these three acceptance routes and links the separate future-payments Direct API guide.
payments-upi-accept-a-payment.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/upi/accept-a-payment, the November change is presentational and navigational (new raw lines 9-16), with no substantive operation or prerequisite demonstrated. source-stripe-upi-accept-payment.md now lists the three captured paths (old raw lines 8-115, 116-581 and 582-1081). Retain the distinct May Direct API evidence for saving UPI in raw/stripe-upi-set-up-future-payments-2025.md lines 109-121 and 341-374. It does not show a missing November acceptance body or a removed integration. Preserve May INR and e-mandate mode limits, immediate one-off and saving versus delayed absent-customer notifications, the five-minute Checkout QR and failure event, and the independent 24-hour Session lifespan in the Elements with Checkout Sessions guide (old raw lines 18-49, 104-114 and 139-143). Preserve the root index line 7, Stripe index lines 367 and 748, and Real-Time Payments concept line 203 routes, add the source backlink and keep the November raw as navigation. The concept's dated future-payments evidence should remain visible alongside the separate table's unspecified labels.
